body.title: Mobile has been asked for **since 2015**
body.lede: The asks go beyond responsive CSS: a compact, task-shaped view of one alert or incident on a phone.

body.footnote: Comments ask to go from a Slack or PagerDuty alert to a dashboard on a phone, and for a mobile-friendly data payload, not only responsive CSS.

body.text: `elastic/kibana` issues; comment summary from the Adaptive UI field-evidence notes
A user can use Nightshift effectively **without ever opening Kibana** — interacting entirely through Slack, GitHub, PagerDuty, or other external surfaces.
…who’s gonna own this rendering capability, right? Because the schema’s gonna define, like, how we render on Slack, how we render on GitHub, how we render on, like, some other external surface.
Stop writing a renderer per channel. **Write the answer once.**

body.title: Six terms carry the whole design

items.body: The wire document, `{ type: 'view', title?, body: Node[] }`. It says **what** the answer is, never how it looks.
One node type: a Zod schema, a catalog entry, examples, and a renderer per surface.
A vocabulary as a value. Packs compose; duplicate types are rejected by name.
Packs assembled into one validator, one parser, the surfaces, and a view registry.
The document an image is drawn in: size, theme, surround. No frame, no `svg`.
One output format, with `render` and `renderNode`. Every surface is synchronous.

body.title: Isomer owns layout. The host owns **everything with consequences**.
body.lede: That line is what lets an agent author a composition: the host trusts it with layout and nothing else.

steps.title: Dispatch
steps.body: Routes each node to its renderer for the surface, after the primitive’s `sanitize` hook.

body.title: Why it matters
What’s new is the contract, not any one renderer
body.lede: Code, agents, and every channel meet at one typed document.

items.body: Three renderers are mandatory, so every composition has a text and a Markdown form.
The JSON Schema the agent reads is projected from the Zod schema that validates.
Agents author layout only; the host keeps data, auth, and side effects.
Errors are written for a model to repair from, and evals measure it.
HTML and images carry only the styles a render reached.
